Any of the video game versions are fantastic for this kind of thing – you can set up your teams and scenarios to really get mileage out of all the different characters in ways that would be tricky to do with the physical game with real people who may or may not want to play along with you feeling out a character.

One of my favorite things to do is use a team of all unusual characters (i.e., nobody that you'd normally use as a primary damage dealer), and quite often they make unexpectedly good teams. Such a team might not have built-in damage individually, but support and buffs add up…

posts.name: bobbertoriley
posts.cooked:
I'll keep it in mind!

Rephrasing my support claim-- NightMist is probably one of the characters where it's hardest for me to juggle the concept of "play what you have" versus "play what you want to have". I think of her like Absolute Zero, where I want to b-line for her equipment immedeately, and before I have that setup going, I rarely want to play spells. And by the time I have her set up, most of the other damage heavy characters are ready and I move more towards playing cards like Mistbound, Planar Banishment, or Enlightenment to help others out.

TL;DR: I usually play NightMist as a slow, set-up build and should try taking more risks. :)

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
One thing that sets Nightmist apart from AZ is while AZ has one way to recoup his HP, Nightmist has several -- the Starshield Amulet, Master of Magic and Mist-Fueled Recovery.

While having the Amulet out is her ideal state, she's perfectly playable and useful without it, thanks to those three. As the guide points out -- the only meaningful HP value is zero, so I'm perfectly comfortable using spells right off the bat in the first couple rounds until I see the Amulet or one of the above cards. I've had whole games where I didn't get Starshield, Amulet or MoM out (or couldn't keep them out), but a late-game MFR got me back in health to keep contributing.

But yeah. Experiment, see what works.
